source_file: hermes_agent-0.19.0-py3-none-any.whl (10,144,439 bytes, sha256 bd0bac012aee38a60894781f4597dc29ee7bedb3448540249921f10d3bef327f, fetched from PyPI files.pythonhosted.org). Opened with Python's zipfile and read in place; requires_python is <3.14,>=3.11, so it was never installed into MCC's 3.14 venv.
note: A rule, not a schema. Hermes Agent publishes no machine-readable schema for config.yaml, so every entry below is a fact read out of the shipped source. It governs a Coding agents CLI launcher (mcc-hermes), not a Desktop apps Configure card.

home_resolution.evidence: hermes_constants.py:46-67: _get_platform_default_hermes_home() returns Path(LOCALAPPDATA)/'hermes' on win32 (falling back to Path.home()/'AppData'/'Local'/'hermes' when LOCALAPPDATA is empty) and Path.home()/'.hermes' elsewhere; _hermes_home_from_env() returns Path(HERMES_HOME) when that is set, else the platform default.
home_resolution.why: MCC writes one file into somebody else's directory. Writing one path while the CLI reads another fails silently, as a picker that never shows MCC's models -- and on Windows the CLI's home is not the user's home at all.

config_document_evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:749-751: get_config_path() -> get_hermes_home() / 'config.yaml'. The same directory holds .env, auth.json and SOUL.md (config.py:753-755).
provider_root_evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:5224-5271: get_compatible_custom_providers() reads config['custom_providers'] (the legacy list, auto-migrated at config version 12) and then providers_dict_to_custom_providers(config['providers']). MCC writes the keyed schema.
provider_keys_evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:5015-5037: _KNOWN_KEYS in _normalize_custom_provider_entry. `unknown = set(entry.keys()) - _KNOWN_KEYS - set(_CAMEL_ALIASES.keys())`; entries in `unknown` are logged as `providers.<name>: unknown config keys ignored: ...` (deduplicated per provider and signature) and then dropped. So an unknown key is not fatal and is not silent -- it is a warning MCC must not cause in somebody else's tool.
required_provider_keys_evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:5055-5075: the base URL is taken from api, url or base_url, validated with urllib.parse.urlparse, and `if not base_url: return None` -- the provider entry is dropped whole, with a warning. `name` defaults to the mapping key (5077-5086), so it is not required.

credential.form: an environment-variable NAME, never a value
credential.evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:5088-5091 keeps key_env as a stripped string; providers.py:625-641 turns it into ProviderDef.api_key_env_vars; agent/auxiliary_client.py:4253-4255 and 5009-5011 read it with os.getenv(key_env). Nothing on disk resolves it.

transport.evidence: hermes_cli/providers.py:38 `transport: str = "openai_chat"  # openai_chat | anthropic_messages | codex_responses`; :401 TRANSPORT_TO_API_MODE maps openai_chat -> chat_completions; :633 `entry.get("transport", "openai_chat")`; hermes_cli/config.py:5099-5101 reads api_mode or transport.

base_url.therefore: api must end in /v1 for transport openai_chat -- the OpenAI SDK appends chat/completions and inserts no /v1 of its own
base_url.evidence: agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1626 builds the URL as f"{agent.base_url.rstrip('/')}{'/responses' if agent.api_mode == 'codex_responses' else '/chat/completions'}".
base_url.mcc_writes: <proxy root>/v1, substituted for a sentinel on the way to disk (config/harness_config_merge.with_base_url)

models.evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:5107-5132: a dict is kept as-is; a list is converted to the dict shape (str items become {id: {}}, dict items take id or name and keep the rest as meta). The dict is what the shipped code expects, so MCC writes it.

per_model_keys_consumed.context_length: The only per-model key the shipped code reads. hermes_cli/config.py:5467 (`raw_ctx = model_cfg.get("context_length")`) inside get_custom_provider_context_length, called from agent/agent_init.py:1765-1775. Separately, agent/agent_init.py:1729 reads the GLOBAL model.context_length (`_config_context_length = _model_cfg.get("context_length")`), which is not the provider block. The provider-level context_length is config.py:5135-5137 and is kept only when int > 0.

per_model_keys_mcc_must_not_write_eviden: None of these is read from a providers.<name>.models.<model> entry by the 0.19.0 code. answer_in_reasoning and prompt_caching appear only in Hermes' documentation of the model page, not in the shipped source.

default_model.evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:5103-5106: `model_name = entry.get("model") or entry.get("default_model")` becomes the provider's model. MCC writes default_model only; it never sends -m/--model on every launch, because hermes_cli/_parser.py:131-145 documents that flag as a per-invocation override ('Applies to -z/--oneshot and --tui').

extra_headers.evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:5150-5155 normalises entry['extra_headers'] with normalize_extra_headers (:5339-5353), which stringifies keys and values and drops None; get_custom_provider_extra_headers (:5356+) returns it for the matching base URL, and the client sends it on every request. MCC writes its x-mcc-harness label here.

rewrites_its_own_document_evidence: hermes_cli/config.py:7515+ save_config writes through utils.atomic_yaml_write (:227-280), a PyYAML dump with default_flow_style=False -- comments and layout are lost. _config_version is DEFAULT_CONFIG's own (config.py:3487 sets 33) and check_config_version (:5490-5523) migrates an older on-disk value, rewriting the file.
undo_implication: Undo cannot promise to restore the bytes Hermes itself rewrote. MCC's own edits are byte-preserving (config/document_codecs), but Hermes' dumper is not, so RESTORE is hash-guarded and refuses when the document moved, and KEYS_ONLY must work with no record at all.
